items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I went around there, John Pantone, took the job, and went to come on with me and went to play it.

ctx.x: But he could play trumpet. I never knew, if somebody told, mention the name of other, just, you knew what he was

about. Yeah, yeah, yeah, I tell ya, I tell ya, he was about, he played trumpet before Joe. I mean, he could play dance music. John Pendleton, he lived uptown, way uptown, too, on, I think he lived up on Pendleton Street. He lived up there. Way uptown. Yeah, yeah. And, uh, Joe Oliver had a repair shoe shop uptown. That's, he started, he had, you know, one of the little repair shoe shops. Well, Joe was playing, uh, brass band music. He could play the trumpet, but he couldn't play nothing but, uh, brass band. You…
Did you ever run with Wooden Joe much?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: So anyhow, he, he, he recommended him to me and I got him and he played the job.

ctx.x: Yeah. But sometime he would play in the brass band, he played baritone. Yeah.

So anyhow, he, he, he recommended him to me and I got him and he played the job. Yeah. Now Joe Oliver didn't, couldn't play no brass band music. I mean, no dance music. No dance. No dance music, but he played brass band music. And right after that, Joe Oliver began to pick up the dance music. Next thing I heard, he was able to play. That's when he went and worked Butler.
Mm-hmm. Waked out on, uh, uh, uh, town on the big avenue. Oh, he was Butler. Yeah.
